newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to ease bond issues-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to ease bond issues-newspaper.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry plans to make it easier to issue corporate bonds by doing away with cumbersome regulations on flotations, the business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Sunday.

The newspaper said the changes, expected to be introduced in 1998 as part of overall economic deregulation measures, were aimed at making Japan's primary market for corporate bonds as free as U.S. and European markets.
Under the new system, which already operates overseas for the issue of so-called medium-term notes, companies will be able to issue new bonds flexibly and reduce flotation costs.

The planned system will give companies three- to five-year quotas for bond issues. Within the quotas, they can float new bonds without going through the present procedure of authorisation by board meetings and public disclosure of relevant information.
The newspaper said the new system would allow issuers to float bonds promptly to take advantage of falls in interest rates.
